# WeldingCalc

Free welding thickness and amperage calculator: TIG amps by material and thickness, MIG wire size and settings, stick rod selection, and machine duty-cycle runtime math. Published rule-of-thumb charts (rod diameter ≈ half base-metal thickness, ~1 A per 0.001" mild steel), computed — no signup.

## Pages
- / — welding thickness & amperage calculator (TIG, MIG, stick, duty cycle)
- /quarter-inch-steel.html — what size welder for 1/4 inch steel
- /mig-or-tig-sheet-metal.html — MIG or TIG for 16–20 ga sheet metal
- /best-beginner-welder.html — best beginner welder by thickness

## Guides
- /how-to-weld-aluminum.html — TIG tab uses Miller’s 90–120 A 6061 butt start at 1/8 inch; other thicknesses use a published Lincoln row or the nearest one
- /what-is-arc-welding.html — OSHA fusion types, then one thickness in three processes
- /how-to-weld.html — measure, rod window, then duty cycle
- /how-to-get-into-welding.html — BLS education, pay, and outlook
- /how-to-clean-metal-before-welding.html — coatings off, then 7018 versus 6011
- /how-to-weld-carbon-steel.html — Miller’s 125 A example versus this MIG tab
- /how-to-choose-a-stick-welder.html — 90–140 A versus the 175–250 A stick class
- /how-to-weld-galvanized-steel-safely.html — zinc-fume controls before any amp
- /how-to-tig-weld-stainless-steel.html — TIG tab 0.9 factor beside Lincoln L16988 stainless column
- /stick-welding-amperage-chart.html — windows stored in the stick tab, not a manufacturer diameter chart
- /what-to-wear-when-welding.html — OSHA 1910.252 shade rows by electrode size
- /welder-duty-cycle-amperage-chart.html — hobby and farm nameplates: process, input voltage, amp range, rated duty cycle
- /embed-calculator.html — embed the thickness calculator; the embed frame itself is noindex

## Questions
- /what-size-welder-for-1-8-inch-steel.html — 125 A for 1/8 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-3-16-inch-steel.html — about 190 A for 3/16 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-3-8-inch-steel.html — 375 A single-pass math for 3/8 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-1-2-inch-steel.html — 300+ A chart row for 1/2 inch steel
- /what-size-welder-for-10-gauge-steel.html — 135 A for 10 gauge (.135 in)
- /what-size-welder-for-16-gauge-steel.html — 60 A for 16 gauge (.060 in)
- /what-size-welder-for-18-gauge-sheet-metal.html — 48 A rule and roughly 70 A for 18 gauge
- /what-size-welder-for-auto-body-panels.html — .023 wire, 30–130 A, for auto body panels
- /what-size-welder-for-aluminum.html — 18 gauge to 3/8 inch aluminum with a spool gun
- /what-size-welder-for-trailer-hitch-repair.html — 200–250 A MIG or 175–250 A stick for trailer hitches
- /what-size-welder-for-farm-repair.html — 130–150 A light farm repair, 200–250 A heavy
- /what-size-welder-for-120v-outlet.html — 90 A at 20% or 115 A at 20% on a 120 V outlet
- /what-size-welder-for-beginner-home-garage.html — 25–140 A or 30–230 A for a beginner home garage
